title: Seifert matrices and the Alexander module

items.title: S-equivalence of integral Seifert matrices

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A–8.B
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3
Knot Theory Lecture Notes, Chapter 7: Seifert Matrices and Derived Invariants
Knot Theory Lecture Notes, Chapter 7: Seifert Matrices and Derived Invariants

items.statement:
Let $V$ be an even-order square matrix with integer entries, of size $n=2g$. A unimodular congruence replaces $V$ by $P^TVP$ for an integer matrix $P$ with determinant $+1$ or $-1$. For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ as column vectors and $z\in\mathbb Z$, the two elementary enlargements of $V$ are
$$
E_0(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
E_1(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Two even-order integral matrices are **S-equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of unimodular congruences, elementary enlargements, and reverse elementary enlargements.

items.title: Seifert pairing and matrix of an oriented knot

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

items.title: Well-definedness of the Seifert pairing

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be the ordered integral basis and positive normal push-off convention used to define the Seifert matrix $V$ above. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. For such representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between the positive push-off of $x$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off, and equals the bilinear extension of $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The linking number of two disjoint oriented circle components is symmetric. In particular, the Seifert pairing is a well-defined bilinear map $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$.

items.title: The skew part of a Seifert matrix is the surface intersection form

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{psmallmatrix}$.

items.title: The cut-open cover presentation of the Alexander module

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 7.B
Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.B
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its induced boundary orientation agrees with the given orientation of $K$. Choose a sufficiently small oriented product tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ compatible with the inward conormal of $F$, set $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T=\partial E$, and put $S=F\cap E$. Thus $S$ is a connected properly embedded surface in $E$ and its boundary on $T$ projects to $K$ with degree $+1$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. Choose a product bicollar of $S$ in $E$, with $S_+$ on the $+n$ side and $S_-$ on the $-n$ side, and let $Y$ be the compact cut-open complement with these boundary copies. The inclusion $j:S\hookrightarrow F$ obtained by removing the boundary collar induces an isomorphism $j_*:H_1(S;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Let $\iota_\pm:S\to Y$ be the two collar-face inclusions and define
$$i_\pm:=(\iota_\pm)_*\circ j_*^{-1}:H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(Y;\mathbb Z).$$
Form a space $\widetilde E_F$ from copies $Y_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$) by gluing $S_-(Y_n)$ to $S_+(Y_{n+1})$ for every $n$, with the remaining boundary faces glued by the inherited product collar. Let $t$ be the deck shift $Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$, which is the shift of the positive meridian, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $Y$ is connected, $\partial S$ is the preferred longitude, and the linking-evaluation map
$$H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z),\qquad [\gamma]\longmapsto\bigl([a]\mapsto\operatorname{lk}(\gamma,a)\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism. There is an exact sequence of $\Lambda$-modules
$$
H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\xrightarrow{i_- -t i_+}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\longrightarrow H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow0,
$$
Thus $H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)$ is the cokernel of the displayed map.

items.title: Seifert matrices of ambient-isotopic pairs are S-equivalent

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3
Knot Theory Lecture Notes, Chapter 7: Seifert Matrices and Derived Invariants

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(K,F)$ and $(K',F')$ be oriented knot and spanning-surface pairs in the oriented standard three-sphere, and let $h_t:S^3\to S^3$ be a smooth ambient isotopy with $h_0$ the identity, $h_1(K)=K'$, and $h_1(F)=F'$, preserving the given orientations. If $V$ and $V'$ are their Seifert matrices in any integral bases, then the basis transported by $h_1$ has matrix $V$, and any other target basis with transition matrix $P$ has matrix $V'=P^TVP$. Hence $V$ and $V'$ are S-equivalent, meaning they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two elementary rank-two enlargement moves or their reverses.

items.title: The Seifert-matrix map in the infinite cyclic cover

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A–8.B
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere, and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary orientation equal to that of $K$. Let $g\ge0$ satisfy $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose a small product tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ adapted to the inward conormal of $F$, put $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $S=F\cap E$, and cut $E$ open along a product bicollar of $S$ to obtain the compact cut-open complement $Y$. Orient the normal line $n$ of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positive in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$; name the face on the $+n$ side $S_+$ and the face on the $-n$ side $S_-$. Let $j:S\hookrightarrow F$ be the collar-removal inclusion and $\iota_\pm:S\to Y$ the two face inclusions; the inclusion induces an isomorphism on $H_1$, and set $i_\pm=(\iota_\pm)_*\circ j_*^{-1}$. Form $\widetilde E_F$ from copies $Y_n$ by gluing $S_-(Y_n)$ to $S_+(Y_{n+1})$, and let $t:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ be the deck shift. Because the boundary orientation of $F$ agrees with $K$, this shift is the positive-meridian shift. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and let $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, where $a_i^+$ is the positive normal push-off. In the linking-dual basis given by $[\gamma]\mapsto([a]\mapsto\operatorname{lk}(\gamma,a))$ under $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$, the map $i_- - t i_+$ is represented over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ by $V-tV^T$. Consequently $H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)$ is the cokernel of $V-tV^T$.

items.title: A Seifert matrix presents the one-variable Alexander module

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 7.B–8.C
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Section 6.2.3

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary orientation equal to that of $K$, let $g$ satisfy $\chi(F)=1-2g$, and choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Use the positive normal convention $(n,u,v)>0$ and define $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module of the knot complement $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, where the cover is classified by the total-linking homomorphism and $t$ acts by the deck transformation corresponding to the positive meridian. Then there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$-modules
$$
A_K\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(V-tV^T:\Lambda^{2g}\to\Lambda^{2g}\bigr).
$$

items.statement: Every Seifert matrix of an oriented knot has positive order, meaning that its number of rows and columns is at least one.

items.title: Trefoil Seifert matrix and basis changes

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links, Chapter 8.A–8.B
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, Example 6.2.11 and Theorem 6.2.9

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and take the genus-one Seifert surface for the trefoil described as $K_1$ in Cattabriga–Francaviglia, Example 6.2.11. In their basis $f_1,f_2$, their negative-first Seifert form has matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, and they identify $K_1$ as the trefoil. Their convention is $\alpha(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^-,y)$; the positive-first convention here is $\theta(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$. In the swapped basis $a_1=f_2$, $a_2=f_1$, the positive-first Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V-V^T=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(V-tV^T)=1-t+t^2.
$$
The determinant-one basis change $P_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ gives $P_0^TVP_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. It changes the off-diagonal entries but not the diagonal entries. The determinant-one basis change $P_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$ gives $P_1^TVP_1=\begin{pmatrix}3&5\\4&7\end{pmatrix}$, changing every entry. For either $P$, the transformed Alexander presentation matrix is $P^T(V-tV^T)P$, so it presents an isomorphic $\Lambda$-module.
